title: Getaway to Bhutan | FREE Hike to Taktsang Monastery
highlights: Enjoy a blend of tradition and nature as you explore Phuntsholing’s gateways, Thimphu’s sacred monasteries, and Paro’s scenic valleys on an amazing journey to Bhutan.
Marvel at the magnificent Buddha Dordenma, a towering statue built to promote world peace, offering a serene retreat amidst the Himalayan landscape.
Hike to the legendary Tiger’s Nest Monastery, where legend says Guru Rinpoche meditated, making it one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations of Bhutan.
Explore the National Memorial Chorten, one of Bhutan’s most important landmarks, where spinning prayer wheels and murmured mantras create a peaceful ambience.
Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve, a conservation centre dedicated to protecting Bhutan’s national animal, offering a rare chance to see these legendary creatures up close.
overview:
About the tour:
Embark on a 5-day journey through Bhutan with a seamless transfer to Phuntsholing, the starting point of your adventure. Discover the cultural heartbeat of Thimphu, where you’ll indulge in the warmth of Bhutanese hospitality and authentic flavours. The tour's highlight is a visit to Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest Monastery, perched dramatically on a cliffside. Let the spirituality and breathtaking views captivate your soul. This tour offers a carefully curated blend of enchanting experiences, ensuring a deep and intimate connection with Bhutan’s unique charm.

know_before_you_go: The updated price is valid only for bookings with 4 adults.
Upon arrival, ask your guide to assist in purchasing a SIM card. Bhutan operates two networks: B-Mobile and TashiCell.
Obtain a visa for each night of your stay in Bhutan, as it's mandatory for all international travellers.
Ensure you have sufficient cash in Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN), especially for remote areas, as ATMs and card facilities may be limited.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.
Images are for representation purposes only.
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Upon your arrival at Siliguri Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport, get driven to your hotel in Phuntsholing. Check in and spend your time at leisure. You can visit Bhutan Gate, a striking traditional gateway that beautifully marks the entry into Bhutan. If you wish, you can also visit Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre lets you witness Bhutan’s wildlife conservation efforts up close, among other famous attractions.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: Today, check out from the hotel and visit the immigration office to obtain your travel permit. Next, get driven to your hotel in Thimphu. After checking in, take the day to explore at your own pace. You can visit Clock Tower Square to admire the beautiful Bhutanese architecture, or immerse yourself in the nation’s history at Simply Bhutan. If you’re a nature lover, you can explore the Royal Botanical Garden to see the variety of plant life. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get driven for a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. First, admire the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa that celebrates Bhutan's third king. Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve to catch a glimpse of Bhutan’s national animal. Marvel at the enormous golden Buddha Dordenma statue & later, explore the Tashichho Dzong, a fortress-monastery that houses several temples and chapels. After visiting other places, get driven to Paro & upon arrival, check in to the hotel.

days.title: Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
days.desc: Today, check out and get transferred to the base of Tiger’s Nest Monastery. Begin your hike, which takes you through lush pine forests adorned with colourful prayer flags fluttering in the breeze. The trek offers stunning views of the surrounding valley and the monastery perched high on a cliff, at 3,120 meters above sea level. Once at the monastery, step inside & explore its prayer wheels, intricate murals, and stunning artwork. Afterwards, get driven back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: After you check out in the morning, get driven to Phuntsholing. After you arrive, check in at the hotel. Later, you can spend your time exploring places like Zangto Pelri, a replica of Guru Rinpoche’s celestial abode. Alternatively, you may admire stunning views from Karbandi Monastery, where lush gardens & prayer flags create a peaceful escape. While exploring the town, you can try Bhutanese dishes like Ema Datshi (chilli cheese) & momos at local eateries, before returning back to the hotel.
